feedback.problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{6x-25}{x(x+5)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{(x+5)},
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are real constants, calculate $A+B.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$ and $B$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6x-25}{x(x+5)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{(x+5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides by $x(x+5)$ gives

$$
6x-25=A(x+5)+B(x).
$$

For $x=0$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6(0)-25 & =A(0+5)+B(0) \\ -25 & =5A \\ A & =-\frac{25}{5} \\ A & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=-5$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6(-5)-25 & =A(-5+5)+B(-5) \\ -55 & =-5B \\ B & =\frac{-55}{-5} \\ B & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
A+B=-5+11=6.
$$
